title: Five Writs: Five Ways to Reach a Court

endcard.line: Pictures: TuckDB (CC BY 4.0); unknown (public domain); Beohar Rammanohar Sinha; David Castor (public domain); MohitSingh (CC BY 3.0)

segments.say: If the State takes away your fundamental right, you can go straight to the Supreme Court. Dr Ambedkar called this right the heart and soul of the Constitution.

right.title: Article 226
items: Rights and any other legal right

segments.say: The Supreme Court hears writs under Article thirty-two, for fundamental rights. High Courts, under Article two twenty-six, can hear them for other legal rights too.
A writ is a court's order. There are five, each with a Latin name and one job.

anim.title: The five
items: Habeas corpus: 'produce the body', free a person held unlawfully
Mandamus: 'we command', make an official do their duty
Prohibition: stop a lower court going beyond its power
Certiorari: quash a lower court's order
Quo warranto: 'by what authority?', remove someone from an office they can't hold

segments.say: Habeas corpus frees a person held unlawfully. Mandamus orders an official to do their duty. Prohibition stops a lower court before it oversteps. Certiorari quashes its order after. Quo warranto asks: by what right do you hold this office?
Students often mix up two. Prohibition comes before a decision, to stop it. Certiorari comes after, to cancel it.
Mandamus can't be issued against the President or a Governor, or a private person. Habeas corpus can be used even against a private person holding someone captive.
For GS Two and Prelims: Article thirty-two and two twenty-six, five writs, and prohibition before, certiorari after.

sources: Constitution of India, Article 32 (right to constitutional remedies; writs in the nature of habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari) and Article 226 (High Courts, for fundamental rights 'and for any other purpose')
Constituent Assembly Debates, 9 December 1948: Dr B.R. Ambedkar on Article 32 (then draft Article 25) as 'the very soul of the Constitution and the very heart of it'
NCERT Class 11, 'Indian Constitution at Work', ch. 2; standard text on writs: mandamus not against the President or Governors or private persons; habeas corpus lies against private persons

quiz.q: Which writ asks 'by what authority' someone holds a public office?
quiz.why: Quo warranto tests the right to hold an office.

quiz.q: Which writ cancels a lower court's order already made?
